::: {.why}
Everything since day 50 was preparation for this hour, which is the first time you take a result you would like to be real and put it against a threshold you set before you had it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the trend follower's Sharpe with an interval, its permutation p-value, and its position relative to your noise floor.
- State the verdict in a form that would read the same if it had come out the other way.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Run the full evaluation: Sharpe with interval from qlib.stats, block bootstrap interval at your chosen block length, permutation test against the block-preserving null, and the same strategy run on 500 synthetic paths from qlib.simulate to get the false positive rate of the procedure itself.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Write the verdict paragraph into reports/milestone-03-pairs.md. Include the number of variants tried, taken from research_log.jsonl and not from memory, and the deflated Sharpe at that count. If the strategy fails, that paragraph is finished work and not a setback.
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The first strategy in the book: a 12-month time-series momentum rule, evaluated against the noise floor from milestone 2 rather than against zero. The evaluation path it runs through is the one every later signal uses, so getting it right once is worth the hour.
:::

## Resources

- [Bailey & López de Prado (2014) — The Deflated Sharpe Ratio](https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

A written verdict on the trend follower in reports/milestone-03-pairs.md, with Sharpe, interval, permutation p-value, trial count and deflated Sharpe.
